meta_description: How to govern AI agents, by Nikhil Singhal. One sales contract moves across teams and companies in nine steps. Each handoff passes through a policy gate.
overview: The picture follows one contract from a company to its customer and back. A salesperson's AI agent drafts it. Experts write their judgment down as policy in step 1. Both companies sign in step 8. In step 9 a question goes back to the experts.

Each time the work changes hands, AI governance kicks in. The picture shows it as a policy gate. The gate reads the intent: who asked for the work, why and on whose authority. Then it enforces the policies that apply. The work goes through, escalates to a person in the loop, or stops. Each decision goes into the audit trail with its reason.
The nine steps below follow the numbers on the picture.
govern_line: Four of the pieces do the work. Govern enforces policy at every gate and keeps the audit trail.

sections.heading: Why it's needed
paragraphs: AI agents now do work for people. They draft contracts and pull customer records. An agent follows the instructions in front of it. It usually can't tell who set a policy or why.
AI governance is how a company keeps that work inside its policies. It also lets the company show later who decided what and why. Today a lot of it is a policy on paper and an audit after the fact.

sections.heading: Where it has to happen
paragraphs: An agent inside a team works under that team's policies and limits. A salesperson's agent can offer only what that salesperson may offer. Trouble starts when work changes hands. A contract goes from Sales to Legal. Then it goes out to the customer. The policies change at each handoff. The reason behind the request can get lost along the way. My view is that governance has to happen at each handoff.

sections.heading: What I'm building
paragraphs: I'm building five products that work together. They let a company hand work to AI agents and still check that the work kept to its policies. Each one has its own section below the picture. You can use CenterEye today. Parts of three others already run. CenterGovern does the checking at each handoff. It isn't built yet.
